title: LLM-assisted security intake and escalation playbook for enterprise questionnaires
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an LLM-assisted intake and escalation workflow to dramatically reduce manual triage time for enterprise security and compliance questionnaires (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR, DPA, vendor RFI). The system will automatically extract questions/clauses, map them to our canonical evidence catalog, generate a risk-first priority score, and recommend an assessor (automated doc vs. human SME). Goal: cut initial TTI for enterprise asks from days to hours and reduce repeated reviewer effort.
proposal: 1) Run a lightweight extraction model on incoming questionnaire PDFs/Word/Forms to identify question clusters and data residency flags. 2) Map extractions to a canonical taxonomy (evidence type, data class, control owner). 3) Compute a triage score combining: customer tier, data sensitivity, legal/regulatory footprint (GDPR/HIPAA), and confidence of automated evidence match. 4) Surface recommended responses and evidence bundles in the new Intake Console; provide an 'escalate to SME' action. 5) Capture feedback loops (SME corrections feed model retraining) and audit logs for compliance.
acceptance_criteria: Automated extractor ingests PDF/CSV/Docx and extracts question+context with >= 85% F1 on a 200Q test set
Taxonomy mapping returns a canonical evidence match in top-3 suggestions >= 80% of time
Triage score aligns with SME baseline (Kendall tau >= 0.6) on a 100-case validation set
Intake Console surfaces recommended evidence bundles and an 'escalate' action with an SLA counter
Audit log entries include extraction confidence, mapping version, and final owner for every processed questionnaire
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Proof-of-concept extractor using off-the-shelf OCR + open LLM for extraction, wire outputs to a staging intake UI. Phase 2 (4 weeks): Build taxonomy mapper, scoring heuristics, and evidence bundle store; add manual correction UI and feedback pipeline. Phase 3 (2 weeks): Integrate with ticketing (Zendesk/Jira) and enterprise console routing; enable canary on pilot accounts. Phase 4 (ongoing): Retrain extraction models, expand regulatory ruleset, add RBAC and audit hardening for Private deployments.
risks: False positives/negatives from automated extraction could misclassify high-risk asks
Regulatory/legal teams may require deterministic provenance that LLMs struggle to provide
Performance: large PDFs may spike processing time and cost without effective preprocessing
Data residency concerns when using hosted LLMs for customer-supplied questionnaires
mitigations: Fallback to human-in-loop review for triage score >= threshold or low confidence
Embed extraction provenance and link each suggested answer to source snippet and OCR confidence
Introduce size-based prefilters and chunking plus async processing with customer-facing SLA
Offer Private deployment option for high-regulatory customers; use on-prem extractor models and KMS for keys
expected_outcomes: Reduce average first-response time for enterprise questionnaires by 60% for pilot customers; lower manual reviewer load by 40%; create a reusable evidence bundle library; improve customer satisfaction (NPS lift in pilot accounts).
notes: We evaluated two extractor approaches: (A) rule-based OCR + regex mapping (fast, brittle), (B) LLM-assisted extraction with few-shot prompts (more robust but requires proven provenance). Team recommends option B with strong provenance metadata.
SME interviews (legal + security) indicated top priority is 'clear mapping to evidence' rather than fully automated answers; UI must highlight confidence and source text.
Parallel effort: ENG-7781 is implementing an evidence-bundles storage API that this feature will consume; coordinate schema changes early.
